content.overview: Multiplication is a multi-trait decision. More shoots can accompany callus, weak morphology or poor downstream rooting, and different genotypes may rank treatments differently.

vocabulary.definition: Propagation using existing buds or meristems.
Formation of new organs from cultured tissue, sometimes through callus-associated pathways.

sections.title: Route affects purpose and risk
sections.body: Axillary multiplication, direct regeneration and callus-associated routes support different production or research goals and create different fidelity questions.

sections.title: Quality is more than count
sections.body: Useful comparisons include usable shoots, morphology, callus, multiplication rate, rooting response and losses. A high count with poor downstream performance may be operationally inferior.

sections.title: Genotype interactions require replication
sections.body: Cannabis studies show genotype-by-treatment effects. Compare identified genotypes with replication and avoid declaring one recipe universally optimal.

workedExamples: Treatment A yields more shoots but twice the abnormal morphology; the choice depends on usable output and later performance.
Cultivar X favors one medium while cultivar Y favors another, so pooled averages can conceal the operational choice.
commonMistakes: Selecting a treatment from shoot count alone.
Ignoring passage or regeneration route in comparisons.
content.practicalApplication: Score two simulated treatments by usable shoots, morphology, callus, rooting, loss and labor, then recommend a controlled next trial for each genotype.
content.summary: Specialist multiplication decisions balance output, quality, route, genotype and downstream performance with replicated evidence.
